history.heading: Discovery and colonisation
paragraphs: Cape Verde, an archipelago of ten volcanic islands in the Atlantic off the coast of West Africa, was uninhabited when Portuguese navigators arrived around 1456–1462. Ribeira Grande (now Cidade Velha) on Santiago, founded in 1462, was the first European colonial town in the tropics and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

The islands became a hub of the Atlantic slave trade, where enslaved Africans were held before being shipped to the Americas. A Creole society formed from the mixing of Portuguese settlers and Africans.

history.heading: Drought and independence
paragraphs: Recurring droughts caused deadly famines, and many Cape Verdeans emigrated, especially to the United States, Portugal and other countries; today more Cape Verdeans live abroad than at home.

Amílcar Cabral led the PAIGC in a joint struggle for the independence of Guinea-Bissau and Cape Verde. After Portugal's 1974 revolution, Cape Verde became independent on 5 July 1975. It became a multiparty democracy in 1991.

culture.heading: Morna and Creole
paragraphs: Portuguese is the official language, but Cape Verdean Creole (Kriolu) is spoken in daily life. Music is central to culture: morna, melancholic songs about longing and emigration, became famous worldwide through Cesária Évora, and is recognised by UNESCO. Other genres include coladeira, funaná and batuque.
Cachupa, a slow-cooked stew of maize, beans and meat or fish, is the national dish. Most people are Catholic.

politics.heading: Stable democracy
paragraphs: Cape Verde is a semi-presidential parliamentary republic and one of Africa's most stable democracies, with regular peaceful changes of power. The prime minister leads the government, while the president is directly elected. The two main parties are the PAICV and the MpD.

economy.heading: Tourism and diaspora
paragraphs: With few natural resources and little rainfall, Cape Verde imports most of its food. Tourism, especially beach resorts on Sal and Boa Vista, is the main industry, and remittances from the diaspora are important.
The Cape Verdean escudo is pegged to the euro. The country has achieved middle-income status and is working to expand renewable energy and the blue economy.
